selection.rationale: Boundary: one coherent editable region covering the complete steady-state pipeline execution - group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb (project.invoke, call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0, all 15 root-only CUDA-graph kernel nodes, 55.745 us inclusive diagnostic CUDA, resources.json 15/15 associated / 0 unassociated) and group 6cbb56a1510e4a69c64d (aten.clone, call d5d112716e884506c96096c0, the per-invocation static_out.clone() fresh-tensor shim, the only observed eager child in the pipeline phase). Both live in the same non-frozen candidate installer; any edit to one must own the other, so they are one joint region. The two remaining groups (d9e5d004d6d24251774f / 798df708d05932b17f71) are profiler record_function enter/exit discovery hooks with 0 CUDA us and no editable pipeline code, so nothing else observed is affected. Coverage is complete and the task is single-device (communication not_applicable), so no measured cost lies outside this boundary. The timing to beat is the accepted revision 02097fcd's clean wall time (parent_values 0.076348/0.076108 ms, reference 0.076228 ms), not the 0.173762 ms original baseline and not the 3.4886 ms hook-perturbed profiled wall time. CONCRETE FAILURE TO REPAIR (previous-feedback decision): trial-resource-audit-c9157758 was rejected for paired_gain_not_above_noise - paired gains [0.005170, 0.016289] ms vs MAD-derived noise bounds [0.006278, 0.012622] ms under the AB/BA fresh-worker protocol where every pair must exceed its bound; pair 0 failed. The feedback shows why: the fused Triton kernel did cut diagnostic GPU time from 55.745 us (15 verbatim kernels) to 6.945 us (1 kernel) and passed quality deterministically (max_abs_error <= 5.7e-7 vs atol=rtol=1e-5 on both continuous steps), but clean wall barely moved and unstably: within-worker samples drift ~0.086 -> ~0.066 ms across the 5 repeats and candidate medians differ by 11.3 us between fresh workers (0.071178 vs 0.059819) while the parent's graph-replay path is stable to ~0.24 us (0.076348 vs 0.076108). The residual ~50-65 us is host-side: the rejected candidate launched the kernel every invocation through Triton's Python JIT dispatch (kernel[grid](...) with per-call specialization/binder work plus torch.empty_like), a CPU-state-sensitive path that both adds tens of microseconds and inflates the MAD noise bounds, so the real 48.8 us GPU saving could not clear the noise test in both pairs. The fix must therefore change the launch path, not the kernel: the accepted parent proves that per-invocation host work consisting of one C++ graph.replay() plus one eager clone is timing-stable on this exact framework and device.
selection.hypothesis: PROMOTE THE QUALITY-PROVEN FUSED KERNEL, BUT EXECUTE IT THROUGH THE STABLE REPLAY PATH THE PARENT ALREADY USES. Build-time (one-time, outside timing): compile the single fused Triton kernel (one program per row of the frozen 256x4096 FP32 workload: affine = x*scale+bias; wave = sin+cos; block-reduce row mean; centered once; block-reduce row variance; normalized = centered*rsqrt(variance+1e-5); output = normalized*sigmoid(normalized)), gate it once against the verbatim eager reference on the prepared inputs at atol=rtol=5e-6 (deterministic kernel, so the gate predicts the framework check), then capture the single kernel launch into a one-node CUDA graph with a static output buffer, identity-guarded to the exact prepared input tensors, and pre-warm with several replays plus synchronize so allocator and clock state are settled before the framework's warmup. Per-invocation timed path: signature/identity guard -> graph.replay() -> return static_out.clone() - i.e. the same C++-class host operations (one replay, one eager clone) as the accepted 0.0762 ms implementation, with zero Triton Python dispatch and zero per-call JIT machinery in the timed loop, which is the specific repair for the pair-0 instability. Fallback chain, chosen once at build and never mid-measurement: any gate failure, capture failure or guard mismatch degrades to the accepted bit-identical 15-kernel CUDA-graph replay path (parity at ~0.0762 ms), never to the reformulated eager var_mean/silu sequence that failed quality deterministically twice (max_abs_error 0.05610130727291107). Expected effect, to be tested by the framework's paired AB/BA measurement (improvement threshold 0.0): GPU work per invocation falls from ~55.7 us of replayed verbatim kernels plus the clone to ~6.9 us fused kernel plus ~3-4 us clone (~10 us total), so CUDA-synced wall latency should move from 0.0762-0.0777 ms toward ~0.030-0.045 ms; even the conservative end is a ~30 us gain, 2.5-5x both observed noise bounds (0.0063/0.0126 ms), with parent-class host stability making both pairs consistent rather than only one. Risks kept explicit: if a Triton kernel cannot be captured into a CUDA graph on the bound device the candidate stays at parity via the fallback (no regression beyond noise); if the fused-kernel gate ever failed, quality is preserved by the bit-identical graph fallback; remaining few-ULP reduction-order/FMA/transcendental deltas are bounded ~5.7e-7 by the already-executed trials, ~18x inside the frozen 1e-5 thresholds.

proposal.rationale: Region rewrite through the project.invoke call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 (adapter.run ABI: runner(state) -> {'output': tensor}), covering both selected groups: 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb (the complete pipeline execution) and 6cbb56a1510e4a69c64d (the accepted bundle's per-invocation static_out.clone() fresh-tensor shim). OBSERVED FACTS: the clean time to beat is the accepted revision 02097fcd's 0.0762 ms (previous-feedback parent_values 0.076348/0.076108, reference 0.076228; original baseline 0.173762 ms, profiled 3.4886 ms wall is hook-perturbed and irrelevant); inside the accepted time, target-resources.json attributes 55.745 us of inclusive diagnostic CUDA to 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 as 15 root-only CUDA-graph nodes replaying the verbatim eager op sequence (~15 full-tensor passes over the 4 MB FP32 tensors), plus the eager clone child and replay/launch overhead. The previous trial trial-resource-audit-c9157758 replaced this with one eagerly launched fused Triton kernel: quality passed deterministically (max_abs_error <= 5.662e-7 on both continuous steps at num_warps 4/8/16 vs atol=rtol=1e-5) and diagnostic GPU time fell from 55.745 us / 15 kernels to 6.88/6.304/9.952 us / 1 kernel, but the bundle was REJECTED for paired_gain_not_above_noise: paired gains [0.005170, 0.016289] ms vs MAD-derived noise bounds [0.006278, 0.012622] ms under the AB/BA fresh-worker protocol where every pair must exceed its bound (pair 0 failed), with within-worker samples drifting ~0.086 -> ~0.066 ms across the 5 repeats and candidate medians differing by 11.3 us between fresh workers (0.071178 vs 0.059819) while the parent's graph-replay path is stable to ~0.24 us. REPAIR (how the previous feedback changes this attempt): keep the quality-proven fused kernel but remove the unstable component - the per-invocation Triton Python dispatch (JITFunction argument binding and launcher, tens of microseconds of host jitter inside the timed region). At build time the single fused launch is captured into a one-node CUDA graph with a static output buffer, gated twice against the verbatim eager reference on the prepared inputs (eager probe, then a zeroed-buffer replay; atol=rtol=5e-6, 2x tighter than the frozen 1e-5), and pre-warmed with three extra replays plus torch.cuda.synchronize so allocator and clock state settle before the framework's warmup. The per-invocation timed path is then identity guard -> graph.replay() -> static_out.clone(): exactly the same C++-class host operations (one replay, one eager clone) as the accepted implementation, with zero Triton Python machinery in the timed loop, which is the specific fix for the pair-0 instability. The kernel still executes on every invocation, reading the live input buffers through replay - nothing is precomputed or cached for the fixture and the work amount is unchanged (one full pipeline computation over the 256x4096 FP32 inputs per run). HYPOTHESIS (tested by the framework's paired AB/BA measurement with improvement threshold 0.0, not an accepted benefit): in-graph GPU time falls from 55.745 us to the previously observed ~6.3-6.9 us while the host-side structure stays matched to the parent's stable path, so CUDA-synced wall latency should move from 0.0762 ms toward ~0.030-0.045 ms; even the conservative end exceeds both observed noise bounds (0.006278/0.012622 ms) several-fold. If the fused benefit does not materialize, the candidate should stay near parity, not regress: the fallback chain is chosen once at build and never switched mid-measurement - any Triton absence, gate failure, capture failure or guard mismatch degrades to the verbatim 15-kernel CUDA-graph replay (bit-identical math to the parent, the accepted revision's own path, ~0.0762 ms parity) and then to the parent reference, never to the reformulated eager var_mean/silu sequence that failed quality deterministically twice (max_abs_error 0.05610130727291107 at 99.9% element mismatch). REPLACES the installed bundle trial-resample-f3c414fc-param-c3d56982, which currently owns the write to 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0; this replacement preserves its whole-pipeline behavior and fresh-output semantics itself. ELIMINATED CALL d5d112716e884506c96096c0 as a distinct parent-observed site: the aten.clone fresh-tensor shim is subsumed into the project.invoke replacement, which performs its own per-invocation static_out.clone() (the same 4 MB device-copy class as the accepted bundle), so observe() still receives a fresh detached tensor with identical values and no consumer changes; the framework's plan recapture will attribute that copy inside the replacement range (the previous trial's diagnostic already showed this group absent_or_unassociated under a candidate-owned runner). Single-device task (communication not_applicable): build returns only this rank's local mapping, no collectives. Parameter num_warps is read from context['parameters'] (default 8, legal values 4/8/16) and only configures the captured kernel's launch/reduction shape; the existing TaskSearch/TPE loop re-measures it under the new graph execution policy - under replay the per-invocation host path is identical for all values, so trials differ only in the in-graph kernel duration - and the selected parameter candidate is independently revalidated with paired project measurements before publication. Optional context['record_route'] is bound with context.get('record_route', lambda *_: None) and invoked inside the replacement on the actually chosen path (labels fused_triton_cuda_graph / verbatim_cuda_graph / parent_delegate); labels are diagnostic self-report only.

setup_work.one_time_build_cost: Primary path: one Triton JIT compilation of a single specialization (WIDTH=4096 constexpr, fp32, num_warps from parameter_space; prior fused trials observed ~0.99-1.06 s installation elapsed), one probe launch into a scratch output, one verbatim eager reference computation for the allclose gate, one static output allocation, three side-stream warmup launches, one CUDA-graph capture of the single kernel launch, one zero + replay + allclose replay-gate, and three pre-warm replays plus torch.cuda.synchronize so allocator and clock state are settled before the framework's warmup. Only the boolean gate outcomes are kept; probe and reference tensors are discarded, and nothing fixture-dependent is cached (the transient gate chain, ~29-30 MB of intermediates, is released to the caching allocator after build - the same transient profile the previous trials showed during installation). Verbatim-graph fallback (built only when Triton is unavailable or a gate/capture fails): side-stream warmup of the verbatim sequence plus CUDA-graph capture, one replay gate and pre-warm replays, matching the replaced bundle's observed ~272 ms install class. No model transformations: the project has no nn.Module roots, no parameters and no caches; the prepared input tensors are read-only (the kernel only loads x/scale/bias and writes candidate-owned buffers).
setup_work.persistent_gpu_memory: Primary path: one retained static output tensor (~4.2 MB for 256x4096 FP32) plus one retained CUDA graph holding a single kernel node with a small graph-private pool; this pool is expected to be smaller than the accepted bundle's pool, which holds the full 15-kernel intermediate chain (~25 MB class) - the exact size is not yet measured and is not claimed as fact. Per invocation the timed path allocates one fresh ~4.2 MB clone from the caching allocator, so warm-run framework.peak_allocated_bytes is expected around the ~12.6 MB class the previous trials observed (prepared inputs + static output + clone: 12615680 B) - parity, not a saving. framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes additionally covers the transient build-time gate chain (~29-30 MB class; prior trials observed 29394944 B), and lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes covers caching-allocator plus retained graph pools (~48 MB class observed, 48234496 B). These are allocator-counter statements, not general physical-memory savings: lifecycle peaks include preparation plus subsequent invocations, warm-run peaks are reset per run, reserved reflects caching-allocator and retained graph pools, and none of the counters measures non-PyTorch driver allocations. Verbatim-graph fallback: a retained graph-private pool holding the verbatim intermediates plus the static output (~25 MB class) with one ~4.2 MB clone per invocation, exactly the accepted bundle's profile (its warm-run peak_allocated can fall when allocation moves into graph capture while reserved pools increase).
setup_work.model_transformations: None. Pure functional project: models(state) returns {}, no optimizer, no gradients, no caches; prepare()'s seeded input tensors are never written; reset() semantics are untouched.

quality_risks: Numerical deltas of the fused kernel are bounded by prior on-device observations, not new claims: max_abs_error <= 5.662e-7 across num_warps in {4,8,16} on both continuous steps (frozen atol=rtol=1e-5), arising from block-tree reduction order, possible single-rounding FMA contraction of x*scale+bias, and libdevice sin/cos/sigmoid/rsqrt lowering; the graph replays the identical deterministic kernel binary (fixed reduction tree, no atomics), so every invocation reproduces the gated values exactly.

Mitigation and repair guarantee: a build-time allclose gate at atol=rtol=5e-6 (2x tighter than the frozen thresholds) runs twice - once on the eager probe (which also performs the one-time JIT compile) and once on a zeroed static buffer after capture - against the verbatim eager reference on the prepared inputs; any failure demotes the whole candidate to the bit-identical verbatim CUDA-graph path (observed max_abs_error 0.0 in the accepted revision's history), never to the reformulated eager sequence whose var_mean-based FP32 mean/variance error (0.087 / 13%) caused the two deterministic 0.0561 failures.

Triton-under-capture risk: the Triton launcher obtains torch's current raw stream and the specialization is compiled and hot before capture (probe plus three side-stream launches), the standard torch.compile/reduce-overhead capture pattern; if capture or the replay gate still fails, the builder resets the graph and falls back to the verbatim graph, keeping parity.

Alias/state semantics: replay writes a candidate-owned static buffer; each invocation returns static_out.clone(), preserving the reference's fresh-output alias semantics (the quality-proven pattern of the accepted bundle, whose clone was the observed d5d112716e884506c96096c0). The path is identity-guarded to the exact captured input tensors; any mismatch or runtime error falls back to the parent reference for that invocation, so external outputs and the {'output': tensor} result structure are always preserved and coverage of 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 is maintained because the replacement callable itself is invoked on every run.

No autograd or state interactions: stateless inference on requires_grad=False inputs; no in-place rewrites of parent-owned storage (the kernel loads x/scale/bias and writes only candidate-owned static_out and its per-invocation clone); no optimizer, cache or collective interactions (single-device request, distributed_backend null).

Parameter exposure is limited to num_warps in {4,8,16}, which only changes the captured kernel's launch/reduction configuration; every value runs the same kernel source, the same double gate and the same fallback chain, so no trial can select the unverified reformulated math.

If the fused path fails its gates on the worker device the candidate remains at parity with the accepted graph implementation rather than risking quality; the fused benefit is then not realized but no regression beyond noise is expected.

params.name: num_warps
params.description: Warps per program for the single fused Triton kernel captured in the one-node CUDA graph (one program per row of the frozen 256x4096 FP32 workload). Changes only the launch/reduction configuration of the captured kernel - never the math, the graph structure, the identity guard or the gates; every value runs the same verbatim-equivalent kernel through the same double allclose gate and degrades identically to the bit-identical verbatim CUDA-graph path on any failure. Under graph replay the per-invocation host path is identical for all values, so trials differ only in the in-graph kernel duration (diagnostic kernel time previously observed 9.952/6.88/6.304 us at 4/8/16 with quality passing at all three).
